action.action-desc: Mr. Cruz (for himself, Mr. Young, Mrs. Blackburn, Mr. Scott of Florida, and Mr. Curtis) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations
Reported by Mr. Risch, with an amendment

form.official-title: To permit visiting dignitaries and service members from Taiwan to display the flag of the Republic of China.

section.header: Requirement to permit dignitaries and service members from Taiwan to display the flag of the Republic of China

subsection.text: The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense shall permit members of the Armed Forces and Government representatives from the Republic of China (Taiwan) or the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO) to display, for the official purposes set forth in subsection (b), symbols of Republic of China sovereignty, including—

paragraph.text: the flag of the Republic of China (Taiwan); and
the corresponding emblems or insignia of military units.

subsection.text: The official purposes referred to in subsection (a) are—

paragraph.text: conducting government hosted ceremonies or functions; and
appearances on Department of State and Department of Defense social media accounts promoting engagements with Taiwan.

section.header: Requirement to permit dignitaries and service members from Taiwan to display the flag of Taiwan

subsection.text: The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense shall permit members of the Armed Forces and representatives from Taiwan or the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO) to display, for the purposes set forth in subsection (b), the following symbols:

paragraph.text: the corresponding emblems or insignia of military units.

subsection.text: The purposes referred to in subsection (a) are—

paragraph.text: appearances on Department of State and Department of Defense social media accounts promoting engagements with Taiwan.

section.text: Nothing in this Act shall be construed as a change to the One China Policy of the United States, which is guided by the Taiwan Relations Act (22 U.S.C. 3301 et seq.), the three United States-People’s Republic of China Joint Communiques, and the Six Assurances.
